summary.oneLiner: RR Kabel delivered record Q4/FY26 revenue and PAT driven by 31% W&C volume growth and pricing, though Middle East geopolitical tensions created a transient export headwind in March/April; the strategic pivot to HV cables (up to 220KV) via INR 1,200cr capex positions it for higher margins and data center/infra orders despite near-term inventory build-up from goods-in-transit.
summary.business: RR Kabel is a wires-and-cables and FMEG manufacturer serving residential, commercial, industrial and infrastructure customers in India and 66+ export countries. The Wires & Cables portfolio (house wires, industrial wires, power cables, specialty cables, solar cables) is the primary business (~90% of revenue), while the FMEG portfolio (fans, lighting, switches, switchgear, appliances and kitchen appliances) is a smaller, distribution-led consumer business (~10% of revenue).

FMEG: Switches & Switchgears (modular switch plates, sockets, regulators, MCBs, RCCBs, Distribution Boards)
Home & Kitchen Appliances (induction/infra-red cooktops, mixer grinders, hand blenders, water heaters, room heaters, irons, air coolers)

currentContext.strengths: One of the broadest international certification portfolios among Indian Wires & Cables manufacturers (42 approvals) providing market-access credentials across 66+ countries|Fully integrated manufacturing model producing its own insulation and sheathing compounds in-house (backward-integrated aluminium rods and compound production), controlling quality at the formulation level rather than just the production line|Loyalty ecosystem of 6,65,000+ electricians and 2,15,000+ retailers that converts the distribution network into a brand-advocacy network|Broad distribution reach of 7,200+ distributors and dealers across India|Management team with deep industry roots and a forward-looking mindset|RR Signature premium sub-brand strategy (60-65% of fan revenue in FY26) capturing the trading-up consumer
currentContext.strategies: Project RRise: a three-year (FY26-FY28) roadmap shifting from broad market expansion to targeted, margin-accretive execution, building healthy sustainable margins through cost optimisation, improved product mix and greater operating efficiency|Re-engineer the W&C product mix to favour the B2B institutional cable market over the retail-heavy wire segment, seeking longer-term contract visibility, stickier institutional relationships and a more predictable cash-flow profile|Deploy capex in modular, biannual tranches at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities calibrated precisely to demand, protecting ROCE by avoiding capital deployment ahead of demand / idle capacity|In FMEG, prioritise high-margin premiumisation over top-line volume; expand the RR Signature premium sub-brand (kitchen essentials - mixer grinders, electric cooktops, hand blenders - launched April 2026)|Deepen B2B partnerships with industrial and corporate customers through wider reach, stronger engagement and consistently reliable, high-quality products|Strengthen export presence in the Middle East and Europe, positioning to benefit from a prospective EU-India trade agreement|Optimise cost structure through renewable energy adoption and automation|Leadership structure realigned to a Joint Managing Director model: Mahhesh Kabra to lead new product development and operational excellence; Rajesh Kabra to lead strategic business development and market expansion (domestic and international)|The Company follows a Dividend Distribution Policy under which the Board declares an interim dividend during the year and recommends a final dividend at year-end, subject to shareholder approval at the AGM, reflecting a stated commitment to creating and sharing value with shareholders alongside continued reinvestment into growth (including the Project RRise capex programme).
currentContext.expansion: Under the three-year 'Project RRise' roadmap (FY26-FY28), RR Kabel committed a three-year capital expenditure programme with the first tranche deployed in FY26 as modular expansions at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities, integrated biannually to align precisely with demand and protect ROCE. Strategic capex was specifically deployed at Waghodia to support the B2B/cable volume scale-up. Separately, capital investments during FY26 upgraded manufacturing infrastructure to add capacity for e-beam cross-linked solar cables (EN 50618 and IEC 62930 certified, UV-resistant, halogen-free) and expanded capacity for fire-resistant, low-smoke cable variants (BS 6724, UL 44, LPCB-certified). On the captive-power side, the Company expanded its hybrid solar-wind renewable energy project during the year, adding 9.6 MW of capacity.

risks.risk: Raw material price volatility (copper, aluminium, PVC/polymers)
risks.note: Copper fluctuated significantly in Q4FY26 and LME copper/aluminium benchmarks remain volatile; management mitigates via long-term procurement contracts, diversified suppliers, dynamic price pass-through in B2C and 100% back-to-back procurement for B2B export orders, but margins remain exposed to sharp swings.

Ongoing Middle East conflict and Red Sea maritime disruptions escalated ocean freight rates, extended transit times and inflated war-risk insurance premiums, and caused an expansion in Sales-in-Transit inventories during the year.

risks.risk: Export / geographic concentration in the Middle East
risks.note: The Middle East contributes approximately 40% of total export revenues (roughly 12% of consolidated revenue), making the Company disproportionately exposed to regional conflict, trade-policy shifts and shipping-route disruption in that geography.
Management explicitly flags intense price competition from both large organised peers and unorganised local players as a threat to margins and market share.
Potential changes in global trade policies and tariff structures in key export markets (alongside evolving US tariff policy) create pricing and demand uncertainty for the export business.

risks.risk: FMEG segment remains loss-making amid a constrained discretionary demand environment
risks.note: Despite narrowing losses (down 28% YoY) and a stated FY27 break-even roadmap, the FMEG segment reported an operating loss in FY26 and operates in a discretionary-spend category exposed to weak consumer sentiment.

one-line thesis: RR Kabel delivered record Q4/FY26 revenue and PAT driven by 31% W&C volume growth and pricing, though Middle East geopolitical tensions created a transient export headwind in March/April; the strategic pivot to HV cables (up to 220KV) via INR 1,200cr capex positions it for higher margins and data center/infra orders despite near-term inventory build-up from goods-in-transit.
financial scorecard: Revenue Q4: INR 2,964cr (+33.7% YoY), FY26: INR 9,722cr (+27.6% YoY); EBITDA Q4: INR 263.5cr (+34.6% YoY, ~8.9% margin), FY26: INR 789.1cr (+61.8% YoY, ~8.1% margin); PAT Q4: INR 168cr (+30.1% YoY), FY26: INR 492.2cr (+58% YoY); Order Book: Not explicitly quantified but described as 'healthy' with high utilization (>90% in cables); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated but working capital described as 'healthy' with tight inventory/receivable control; One-offs: Inventory gain acknowledged as 'positive but marginal/unquantified' due to rising copper prices; SIT (Stock-in-Transit) inflated inventory days by ~2-3 days due to export delays.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~30% FY27 (implied mathematically by 16-18% volume + price rise); Margin: Targeting 9.5% EBIT for W&C in FY27, 10.5% by FY28 (300bps expansion roadmap); Order Inflow: Strong B2B/Infra focus; Capex: INR 1,200cr program (FY26-FY28), INR 300cr spent in FY26, majority spend in FY27.
order book & pipeline: Management cites >90% capacity utilization in cables; no specific value given, but demand described as 'healthy' domestically and 'stronger' in exports excluding Middle East disruption; B2B segment scaling rapidly.
segment / subsidiary detail: Wires & Cables: 90% of FY26 revenue (INR 8,764cr, +31% YoY), Segment Profit INR 776cr (+56% YoY); FMEG: 10% of revenue (INR 959cr, +3% YoY), losses narrowing, breakeven delayed to FY27 (from FY26) due to weather/input cost lag.
growth verticals / optionality: HV/EHV Cable expansion (66KV to 220KV capability) targeting infra/wind/solar/data centers; B2B channel deepening; Export diversification beyond Middle East; FMEG turnaround to breakeven in FY27 with 20-25% value growth target.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material (Copper, Al, PVC) volatility managed via continuous pricing pass-through (2-3% triggers); FY26 margin expansion of 130bps achieved; FY27 guidance 9.5% despite elevated copper base; FMEG margins pressured by input cost lag.
capex / expansion: INR 1,200cr total (FY26-FY28); INR 300cr deployed in FY26; majority outflow in FY27; adds HV capacity (up to 220KV) in phases every 6 months through FY28.
capital allocation: Dividend INR 9.50/share for FY26 (INR 5.50 final); Reinvestment in capacity expansion (Project RRise); Working capital optimization via LC facilities.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension in Middle East (12% of total top line, 40% of exports) causing shipment delays; Copper price volatility impacting working capital and pass-through timing; FMEG breakeven delay; Potential industry capacity addition (though mgmt sees no oversupply risk for their mix).
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural growth (16-18% CAGR); Pragmatic on near-term geopolitical noise; Disciplined on pricing and cost control; Transparent on FMEG delays.
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory bloat is largely 'Stock-in-Transit' (SIT) due to war-related shipping delays rather than demand slowdown; Data center opportunity is immediate using existing product suite (no new R&D wait time) but requires approval cycles; Cable mix shift (27% to ~31%) driven more by volume/capacity than just price, enabling better operating leverage.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain disruption in Middle East and high copper prices | Polycab India | beneficiary | Med | As the market leader, Polycab may capture marginal share if RR Kabel's export logistics remain constrained, though RR's domestic focus mitigates this. |
| Need for HV cables in data centers and renewable projects | KEI Industries | beneficiary | Med | Competitor also expanding HV capacity; sector tailwinds benefit all organized players with execution capability. |
| Input cost volatility and FMEG margin pressure | Unorganized FMEG/Cable Players | loser | High | Inability to pass through costs quickly or access working capital for inventory buildup during price spikes will force consolidation. |

themes.title: Power transmission & renewable-evacuation capex
themes.need: Grid build-out to evacuate ~90 GW of new renewables is the broadest theme in the universe - pulling EHV/765kV transmission EPC, towers, conductors, OPGW, cables and HVDC. POWERGRID/ADANIENSOL TBCB pipeline plus state RDSS/underground-cabling capex (Rajesh Power 544291, OMPOWER) underpins multi-year visibility for EPC, tower (KP Green 544150, SKIPPER) and conductor/cable makers (KEI, RRKABEL, DYCL).
themes.driver: Fresh TBCB awards + execution ramp; EPC order inflows over next 1-2 quarters.

The Wires & Cables portfolio (house wires, industrial wires, power cables, specialty cables, solar cables) is the primary business (~90% of revenue), while the FMEG portfolio (fans, lighting, switches, switchgear, appliances and kitchen appliances) is a smaller, distribution-led consumer business (~10% of revenue).

guidance.body: Revenue Growth: ~30% FY27 (implied mathematically by 16-18% volume + price rise); Margin: Targeting 9.5% EBIT for W&C in FY27, 10.5% by FY28 (300bps expansion roadmap); Order Inflow: Strong B2B/Infra focus; Capex: INR 1,200cr program (FY26-FY28), INR 300cr spent in FY26, majority spend in FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: HV/EHV Cable expansion (66KV to 220KV capability) targeting infra/wind/solar/data centers; B2B channel deepening; Export diversification beyond Middle East; FMEG turnaround to breakeven in FY27 with 20-25% value growth target.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Data centre build-out is a major demand catalyst, requiring markedly higher cable-density per square foot than traditional industrial projects due to redundancy and zero-downtime requirements
- Transition to green energy infrastructure (solar, wind, transmission grid expansion, rural electrification) is creating multi-year demand cycles for specialised cabling
- Domestic economy provided a supportive operating environment (infrastructure capex, affordable housing, EV adoption, rising incomes) even as the global environment was volatile with Middle East shipping disruptions and copper/aluminium/PVC price volatility
- Year-end inventory was elevated due to Sales-in-Transit (SIT) caused by Middle East shipping disruptions; management expects this timing difference to normalise in coming quarters
- Cable volumes are structurally outpacing wire volumes, reflecting a B2B/institutional demand shift; cable lines ran at high utilisation through the year
- Housing wire demand is structurally tied to residential completions, with premiumisation (FR-LSH, energy-efficient variants) and smart-home wiring content (~30% more wiring per home) as additional demand accelerants
- Wire and cable market is formalising, with the organised segment's share rising (regulatory tailwinds: BIS certification mandates, National Building Code fire-safety enforcement, state electricity board compliance audits) at the expense of the unorganised segment
- Specialty and industrial cables are the fastest-growing sub-segment, driven by data centres, pharmaceutical manufacturing, industrial automation and solar/high-voltage grid-tie demand
- Export demand faced Middle East geopolitical headwinds but showed resilience, with the Middle East remaining the core geography for international operations

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Raw material (Copper, Al, PVC) volatility managed via continuous pricing pass-through (2-3% triggers); FY26 margin expansion of 130bps achieved; FY27 guidance 9.5% despite elevated copper base; FMEG margins pressured by input cost lag.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend INR 9.50/share for FY26 (INR 5.50 final); Reinvestment in capacity expansion (Project RRise); Working capital optimization via LC facilities.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Under the three-year 'Project RRise' roadmap (FY26-FY28), RR Kabel committed a three-year capital expenditure programme with the first tranche deployed in FY26 as modular expansions at the Silvassa and Waghodia facilities, integrated biannually to align precisely with demand and protect ROCE. Strategic capex was specifically deployed at Waghodia to support the B2B/cable volume scale-up. Separately, capital investments during FY26 upgraded manufacturing infrastructure to add capacity for e-beam cross-linked solar cables (EN 50618 and IEC 62930 certified, UV-resistant, halogen-free) and expanded capacity for fire-resistant, low-smoke cable variants (BS 6724, UL 44, LPCB-certified). On the captive-power side, the Company expanded its hybrid solar-wind renewable energy project during the year, adding 9.6 MW of capacity.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth (16-18% CAGR); Pragmatic on near-term geopolitical noise; Disciplined on pricing and cost control; Transparent on FMEG delays.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the broadest international certification portfolios among Indian Wires & Cables manufacturers (42 approvals) providing market-access credentials across 66+ countries
- Fully integrated manufacturing model producing its own insulation and sheathing compounds in-house (backward-integrated aluminium rods and compound production), controlling quality at the formulation level rather than just the production line
- Loyalty ecosystem of 6,65,000+ electricians and 2,15,000+ retailers that converts the distribution network into a brand-advocacy network
- Broad distribution reach of 7,200+ distributors and dealers across India
- Management team with deep industry roots and a forward-looking mindset
- RR Signature premium sub-brand strategy (60-65% of fan revenue in FY26) capturing the trading-up consumer

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical tension in Middle East (12% of total top line, 40% of exports) causing shipment delays; Copper price volatility impacting working capital and pass-through timing; FMEG breakeven delay; Potential industry capacity addition (though mgmt sees no oversupply risk for their mix).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory bloat is largely 'Stock-in-Transit' (SIT) due to war-related shipping delays rather than demand slowdown; Data center opportunity is immediate using existing product suite (no new R&D wait time) but requires approval cycles; Cable mix shift (27% to ~31%) driven more by volume/capacity than just price, enabling better operating leverage.
